points.description: States that multiple hidden layers are desirable when deep or hierarchical learning of features is needed: the hidden layers extract and learn features from the data so the network can perform the task well (complex or non-linear patterns).
points.partial_credit: Half a mark for saying more hidden layers help learn features or perform better, without the idea of extracting or learning features from the data, or with only a vague reference to deep learning.

points.description: Gives a suitable example of a case needing multiple hidden layers, such as multiclass classification or the XOR function (a problem that is not linearly separable).
points.partial_credit: Half a mark for an example that is named but not justified, or a plausible example that is not one of the standard cases (for example, a complex non-linear classification problem).

rubric.notes: Full marks need both the idea that extra hidden layers are needed to learn or extract features (deep learning) for complex tasks, and a valid example such as multiclass classification or XOR. Half marks go for a vague feature-learning idea, or an example given without explanation. No marks for answers that say only "more layers are better" with no feature-learning idea and no example, or for unrelated answers such as one hidden layer being sufficient.
